The framework leverages zero-shot learning to detect soccer events without task-specific training. It segments full-length matches into overlapping clips and encodes them into compact visual storyboards. These storyboards enable efficient multimodal reasoning by reducing input dimensions while preserving temporal coherence. The system uses a general-purpose multimodal language model to jointly process visual and textual modalities for event classification and localization. Temporal consolidation ensures consistent event timestamps, while excitement scoring introduces interpretability through natural-language explanations. The core innovation lies in combining sparse frame sampling, storyboard construction, and multimodal reasoning to achieve high F1@5s performance with reduced inference cost. Dualities emerge between visual and textual modalities, where each contributes distinct signal strength to event detection. Failure modes include misalignment of visual and textual cues, poor temporal resolution, or insufficient generalization capacity of the base model.
